findings.evidence: Identical shape and identical proof term already exist as `Tensors/Basic.lean:279 lemma lMuNuOdd_apply ... : lMuNuOdd ε K v w = ε ![v, w, K.k, K.kPrime] := ε.bilinMap_apply _ v w`; the repo's own helper is `AlternatingMap.bilinMap_apply` (Mathematics/LinearAlgebra/Alternating/BilinMap.lean:52), and Mathlib names the analogous alternating-map-equals-determinant lemma `Module.Basis.det_apply` (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Determinant.lean:607), used in this PR at ParityOdd.lean:439.
findings.fix: Rename to `aOfBasis_apply` and `aFour_apply` (no clash with the specialized `aFour_kFour_apply`).
findings.issue: `aOfBasis_eq_det` (and `aFour_eq_det`, line 430) are the pointwise-evaluation lemmas of a bundled bilinear form (`aOfBasis b K v w = b.det ![v, w, K.p, K.q]`), which the convention names `_apply`, not `_eq_<rhs>`.

findings.evidence: Basic.lean:639 `theorem covariant_spectator_offDiagonal_zero ... (hu : g u u ≠ 0) (hup : g u K.p = 0) (huq : g u K.q = 0) (huv : g u v = 0) : W u v = 0` vs Basic.lean:944 `theorem covariant_offDiagonal_zero_of_spectator ... (hu : u ≠ 0 → g u u ≠ 0) (huq) (huT) (huv) : W u v = 0`, whose proof is a case split delegating to the former (line 950).
findings.fix: Keep the established stem and mark the variant, e.g. `covariant_spectator_offDiagonal_zero'`, or encode the distinguishing hypothesis (non-nullity assumed only for `u ≠ 0`, spectator given by orthogonality to `q` and `p_T`).
findings.issue: `covariant_offDiagonal_zero_of_spectator` is the same words as the pre-existing `covariant_spectator_offDiagonal_zero` (line 639) in a different order, with the same conclusion `W u v = 0` under an equivalent spectator hypothesis; neither name tells a caller which of the two it is.

summary: Two naming-convention deviations: the evaluated-form lemmas for the parity-odd structure are named `_eq_det` where the project and Mathlib use `_apply`, and the new spectator off-diagonal theorem permutes the words of the existing one with the same conclusion. Everything else reads from the conclusion in standard terminology.
